newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of NAPM.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of NAPM.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's 1500 GMT release of the U.S. November National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) index and October contruction spending data, dealers said on Monday.
The NAPM index for November is forecast to rise to 50.8 percent compared with 50.2 percent reported in October.
October construction spending is expected to show a decline of 0.1 percent against a 1.9 percent increase reported in September.

"The market was steady to slightly higher in the morning on some position adjustments. We are now waiting for fresh clues about the market from tonight's release of the (U.S. November) NAPM index and (October) construction spending figures," a local dealer said.
"But I don't think there will be much impact as the numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared or are squaring their positions," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Monday/Tuesday rose 3/8 percentage point to 5-7/8 5-3/4 percent.
Tuesday/Wednesday rose 1/4 point to 5-3/4 5-5/8 and week-fixed rose 1/16 point to 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent, respectively.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged at 5-9/16 5-7/17 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-1/2 5-3/8, nine-months unchanged at 5-9/16 5-7/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent.
